meanings: the Aetherbonded ('the mortar-folk of the sky'): the full name, of which et Lodhan 'the Bonded' is the guild's short one
derivation: a construct: canon Lodhan 'the Bonded' (lodh + -an) + S·helv 'the sky' (h unchanged), the definite possessor, as in canon Lodh Helv 'the Aetherbond' (lodh + helv); the head of a construct takes no article (orrowen_v2 §3.2). Made for the foreword ('They are of the Aetherbonded, whom the guild calls simply the Bonded', where et Lodhan alone would make the sentence say the same thing twice) and I.2; unit S01

meanings: the Elder and the Elderess: an elder pair (Halyna, 'the elders of the guild at this Keep'; 'two elders who sat apart')
derivation: a phrase: canon Hemm Elder + eth and + canon Hemma Elderess (one rank: orrowen_v2 §5.2). Used where pa hemm 'two elders' would also be heard as S·cemm, 'two meetings'; unit S01

meanings: wait on, wait for one another ('wait upon'): nath dovv hos um ullen, 'neither waits on the other'
derivation: a phrase: canon tovv wait + canon um upon (+S; a vowel after it shows nothing). The literal 'wait upon'. dem 'until' (I.1's re dhovv o dem hos, 'waited for one') is avoided before ullen, because dem nasalises a vowel-initial word (dem mullen); unit S01

meanings: end a cry, or a line spoken by two: 'lay the lintel on the cry'; the counterpart of cadh et tolm hosast 'begin' ('lay the first stone')
derivation: a phrase: canon hosk (v.) lay the lintel, seal + et the + canon carm a cry. The second voice caps the line as a lintel caps a gate (the pair is a gate, orrowen_v2 §3.10). I.2: Re hadh ey o dholm hosast ... Eth re hosk o et carm, 'She began it ... And he ended it'; unit S01

meanings: between them ('in their mortar'); of two, ul sona lodh 'between them two'
derivation: a phrase: tier-3 ul lodh 'between' (O2632, 'in the mortar of') with the possessive so / sona (+S; l unchanged) set before the noun, as every possessive is (orrowen_v2 §3.5). Said of two cries, and of a line two voices share; unit S01

meanings: the right hand ('the true hand'); lo yarl venn, 'at the right hand, on the right'
derivation: a phrase: canon garl hand + canon venn true (its senses already include 'right; right-hand', O2715); after lo (+S) garl is yarl. The facing leaves of the foreword ('the wood's on the right'); unit S01

meanings: the left hand ('the other hand'); lo yarl ullen, 'at the left hand, on the left'
derivation: a phrase: canon garl hand + tier-3 ullen other (its senses already include 'left (the other hand)', O2649); after lo (+S) garl is yarl. The facing leaves of the foreword ('ours on the left leaf'); unit S01

meanings: facing each other ('one in the face of the other'): of the two facing leaves
derivation: a phrase: hos one + tier-3 ul lern 'in the face of, facing' (O2631) + ullen the other, as the possessor of lern (a vowel shows no softening); built as IV.4's doss o ul lern Yebb et Pard, 'it faces the Warden's Door'; unit S01

meanings: which was which, who was who: nath seskym cedh ew cedh, 'I could not tell you which'
derivation: a phrase: canon cedh who + canon ew was (the copula, past) + cedh. No mutation: cedh and ew cause none, and neither stands after a trigger (after one, cedh would soften to hedh, which is also 'dusk'); unit S01 (I.2)

meanings: Whoever holds it tells: the rule of the tale-stone at the Long Hearth (the foreword and the Invocation)
derivation: a phrase: canon brodh tell + gor sa 'whoever' (gor every + the relative sa: lexicon_orrowen.md §5.3) + heth S·keth hold (after sa) + o it; verb first, the relative clause its subject. brodh, not cadh: the hearth tells with the stone in hand, and the tale is laid when the stone is set back (the foreword); unit S01
title + name: canon Hemma Elderess + canon Rhyna (a name is a name); I.2 ('She was Elderess Rhyna, Rhyna of the Inner Gate'); unit S01
title + name: canon Hemm Elder + canon Halvard (a name is a name); I.2 ('He was Elder Halvard, Halvard Stone-Warden'); unit S01

meanings: Every gun that is hauled is a course of stone not laid ('every hauled gun, a course unlaid'): the siege day's arithmetic (I.2)
derivation: a verbless saying, as Orrowen proverbs are (orrowen_v2 §11.7): gor every (+S) + S·bramm gun + caldat hauled (cald + -At); then, after the wedge, trenn course + nahadhat unlaid (na- + S·cadhat, O1513). No trigger stands before caldat, so the reserve cald keeps clear of hald 'wall' and gald 'build' (lexicon_orrowen.md §8 item 2); unit S01
